title: SYSK Selects: How McCarthyism Works
summary: SYSK Selects rerun episode explaining McCarthyism: the term's definition, Senator Joseph McCarthy's rise and 1950 Wheeling-area "list" speech, the Second Red Scare, the Hollywood blacklist (Red Channels, Waldorf Statement, Hollywood Ten), the Rosenberg case and Venona transcripts, the 1954 Army-McCarthy hearings, McCarthy's censure in 1954 and death in 1957, and historian John Earl Haynes's assessment of those McCarthy named. The episode closes with a contest announcement and a sponsor-free outro.
topics: McCarthy list of State Department employees

segments.title: Selects intro and cold open banter
segments.summary: Josh introduces the Selects episode on McCarthyism, apologizes for outdated language, and the hosts banter about Cheap Trick and the Dixie Chicks' 2003 controversy.

segments.title: Definition and Joseph McCarthy's background
segments.summary: The hosts define McCarthyism per the American Heritage Dictionary and cover McCarthy's early life, Marine service, Senate election, and his shift to attacking alleged communists.

segments.title: The 1950 speech and the list
segments.summary: McCarthy's Lincoln's Birthday speech in West Virginia cited a list of State Department employees; the number of names is disputed (205 versus 57). The hosts discuss McCarthy's alcoholism and rumors about his sexuality.

segments.title: Second Red Scare and anti-communist laws
segments.summary: Context of the Second Red Scare, including China's communist takeover, the Soviet atomic bomb, and the Communist Party USA leaders' conviction. Laws like the Alien Registration Act are discussed, along with political opposition to McCarthy from Truman and Eisenhower.

segments.title: Rosenberg case and Fifth Amendment
segments.summary: Julius and Ethel Rosenberg's execution is discussed, with the later release of Venona transcripts suggesting Julius passed military-industrial information rather than atomic secrets. The hosts discuss how pleading the Fifth Amendment was treated as guilt during McCarthy-era hearings.

segments.title: HUAC and the Hollywood blacklist
segments.summary: The House Un-American Activities Committee's origins and misuse are described. The Hollywood blacklist is covered through Red Channels, the Hollywood Ten, the Waldorf Statement, and individual cases such as Lee J. Cobb, Elia Kazan, and Charlie Chaplin.

segments.title: Impact on culture and the 1954 Army hearings
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the blacklist's human cost, book purges, The Crucible as allegory, and McCarthy's 50 percent favorability. They then cover the televised Army-McCarthy hearings, which turned public opinion against him after Eisenhower and Nixon's involvement.

segments.title: Censure, death, and historical assessment
segments.summary: McCarthy was censured by the Senate in 1954 and died in 1957 of acute hepatitis linked to alcohol abuse. Historian John Earl Haynes's review of the Venona material found that of 159 people McCarthy named, nine were aiding Soviet espionage. The hosts close with modern parallels.

segments.title: Contest announcement and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts announce a now-defunct Facebook contest with a grand prize trip to Atlanta, then give closing contact information and sign off.
